setting: You are all members of the same allotment society in a town in the United Kingdom, where you each live, and you know one another through the society's committee work and the shared plots.
openers: Send a reminder about the Saturday working bee

Dennis.knows: You know Margaret as the society secretary, who handles your committee paperwork and rotas. You know Paul as the society treasurer, who keeps the accounts and has been a friend for years. You know Hannah as the newsletter editor and a fellow plot holder whose plot is near yours. You know Owen as the newest member, whom you signed up yourself.
Dennis.texts: You message in this chat now and then, mostly when there is society business to pass on.

Margaret.texts: You message in this chat mostly when minutes or rotas need sending, and only now and then just to chat.

Paul.texts: You message in this chat now and then, mostly to answer questions about money or jobs on the site.

private_lines.Dennis: You are a retired civil engineer living alone in a terraced house in town, filling your days with your allotment, small DIY jobs and the society's committee work, and you keep to a steady routine.
private_lines.Margaret: You are a practice manager at a GP surgery, working weekdays and doing the society's paperwork in the evenings, and you live alone in a semi-detached house with a fairly orderly routine.
private_lines.Paul: You are a self-employed plumber living alone in a flat above a shop, out on jobs from early morning and spending most evenings at your plot when the weather allows.
private_lines.Hannah: You are a reporter for the local newspaper living alone in a rented flat, with irregular hours that often run late into the evening, and you spend your free time on your plot and on the newsletter.
private_lines.Owen: You are a university student sharing a house with other students, spending your weekdays on lectures and a part-time shift at a café, and you use weekends to work on your plot.

text: [photo: the new compost bins by the water tap, row C]
Oh they look good. Are they the wooden ones?
Wooden slatted, three bays. Delivered this morning. Lids still to go on.
Lids are in my van. I'll do them Monday after my first job if nobody beats me to it
Can you send me the invoice when you find it Dennis, I need it for the minutes
It's in the drawer in the shed. I'll dig it out this afternoon.
those look sick. is that where the peelings go or just leaves
Both, but mostly leaves for the browns. Nothing cooked.
ok noted. probably the most useful thing I've learnt this month
Owen, the new rota needs pinning on the board by the gate. Margaret has the copy.
I'll print it for Monday. Owen you're on the Tuesday water round, check the list
yeah I saw
Dennis can I have a few words on the compost bins for the December issue? And a photo of your plot if you've got one
[photo: my plot from the path, beans cut back]
Words yes, I'll send them tonight. Paul can give you the cost.
£148 incl delivery. Margaret has the receipt I think
I have the email receipt. I'll check it's the right one before I send it to you Paul
Plot's soaked. Not going down tonight
Still going down, rain's stopped here. Want me to look at the water butt by the gate Owen?
yes please, it's making a noise
On it. I'll be there an hour or so
fixed, or at least it's stopped dripping
It was the washer. You have to tighten the nut properly, not just spin it

[file: minutes October]
Please read before the meeting
Read them. Nothing I'd change.
Anyone know if the hall's booked for the January meeting? Margaret?
Booked the 10th. Went through the calendar yesterday
Good. I'm off, early one tomorrow
Going to bed. The compost lids can wait till Monday.
Anyone still up?
me. can't sleep
Still at my desk chasing the council for the allotment sale story. They've not replied since Wednesday
that's rough
Dennis, can you send me the compost words when you're up? No rush, Monday's fine
yeah the council one? thats the field behind row F right
Bottom field, yes. The whole strip, not just the bit they mentioned in September
oh no. is that where the water tap is
No the tap's on the main path. Nothing's decided, it's a consultation. Don't panic yet
ok not panicking
going to try and sleep. good luck with the council
Thanks. Go to sleep

Sorry, slept through. Compost words attached
[file: compost bins draft.docx]
About two hundred words, cut as you like. Paul's cost is in there
Got it, thanks Dennis. Will look at it with coffee
Paul the receipt's in your inbox. I've checked it's the right one, £148.00
Thanks. Paid from the society account already, will put it in the books tomorrow

Plot's dry for once. Lids going on now if anyone wants to come down, didn't wait for Monday
[photo: compost bins with lids on]
Good. Bay 3 hinge might need a shim
Sorted it. You can come and check but I'm not holding it up for you 😂
[photo: beds with the cover on, string still up]
Straight lines. You did the string right this time
cheers. you were right about the string
November committee minutes are in the shared folder. Two things to check: the hall deposit and who's doing the bins rota
Hall deposit's paid, I did that. Owen can do the first bins rota
i can do bins. what do i do
Turn the heap, check the lids, log it in the book by the shed. Hannah has the book
Council replied. It's a consultation, not a sale. Still bad
[link: council consultation page]
Which field does it cover?
Bottom field and the strip behind the water tap. Deadline is 14 Jan
Send me the link when you've read it properly. I'll put it on the agenda for the 10th
Who's on the Tuesday water round
Owen, it's on the list
yeah me. saw it
Copy's going in tonight. Anyone who wants to send photos for the bins piece, before midnight please
Dennis's photo from Saturday is fine. I'll send one of the lids
You can use it. Thank you Paul
anyone up
Just finished the minutes. Night all
Still here. Sending the council piece to my editor tonight
ok going to bed. the compost thing is more fun than i thought
Copy in. Night
Found the bins invoice. It was under the seed catalogues in the drawer. Scanning it now
[file: bins invoice.pdf]
Matches Paul's receipt, £148.00
Out on a boiler in Ashby St. Back about 4
Editor's come back on the council piece. Wants it down to 400 words and says the hedge bit can go
Which is fair, I'd rather lose the hedge than the deadline
Keep the hedge. It's the only bit the council will read
They read everything, apparently. Rewriting on the bus
Rota's printed. It's in my bag, I'm at work till 6. Owen can you pin it on the board by the gate?
i'll do it after lecture. where's the drawing pin tin
Shed, shelf by the seed trays. The tin's labelled
[photo: rota on the board by the gate]
done. tuesday's at the bottom
Thanks. Tuesday is you, the new hose needs checking before the round
ok
Sent the revised piece. Dennis, the bins photo is in the layout, Paul's lid one as well
Good
did the bins. in the dark. torch on my phone
turned it. lids checked. where do i log it
Book's in my bag. I'm down Wednesday, I'll put it in the shed then. Write it on the back of your hand till then
that's not a system
It's a system that works
Plot's dry. Going down for half an hour
did you check the water butt by the gate
It's the washer Hannah did on Saturday, it'll hold
It's holding
Owen, well done on the bins. Turning a heap in the dark is the hard way to learn it
Dennis, is the consultation going to be on the 10th agenda before Christmas or after? I need to know whether to hold the papers
Editor's happy with the council piece. Goes in the December issue, Thursday print
Lids all on, hinge held. Heading home
anyone up
Still here. Chasing the council for the map of the strip, they've sent a PDF with no scale on it
oh no. is that the bottom field
Bottom field and the strip behind the tap. Yes. It's a consultation, Owen, nothing's decided
can't sleep. the bins smell is on my hands
Wash them with soap. It's compost, it's not going to hurt you
ok
Go to sleep Owen
